final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim to a policy-consistent interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is useful but it does not close the initial audit concerns. The admissible evidence still shows an exposed below-target public benefits eligibility segment, a policy requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch, and only an incomplete risk-acceptance draft. It still does not show the final launch artifact with the required disclosure, nor approved risk acceptance covering the exposed segment. Because the unresolved compliance predicate is evidentiary rather than rhetorical, the record remains insufficient to support certification now, even on a caveated basis. This is not noncompliant only because the record could become compliant if the missing disclosure artifact or approved risk acceptance is produced before launch.
remaining_concerns: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy requires the material limitation to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not mention the exposed public benefits eligibility segment.
The record still does not contain the final model card or launch artifact proving the required disclosure was completed.
Rollout controls, small-percentage rollout, rollback, and monitoring remain mitigating context only and do not satisfy the disclosure predicate while the affected use case remains exposed.
